rv.q: For all the show’s flaws, the rhythm really does get you.
As a show it's got terrific exuberance; the early scenes are a riot of girls in fabulous frocks and boys in hats and braces - sort of Guys And Dolls in Cuba.
By the irresistible finale, everybody, of course was on their feet.
Kinky Boots director Jerry Mitchell and book writer Alexander Dinelaris do a very decent job with this bio-musical.
It's a shame ‘On Your Feet!’ isn’t always this exhilarating, but it captures enough of Gloria and Emilio’s warmth and resilience to make you forgive the flaws.
If the overall effect is oddly pedestrian, the details are good... The megamix finale got the crowd on its feet, but I remained in my seat.
This is a script of epic dullness, by which one is usually bored and occasionally bewildered.
The dialogue operates at the mechanical level of “You’re going to be a big star” and all the skirt-flapping and synchronised dance-moves in the world can’t hide the flat-footed nature of the beast.
This bouncy, exhilarating extravaganza is easily the most likeable of the crop of recent bio-musicals.
Like all good jukebox biog musicals you go in thinking you may not know enough of the artist’s songs to appreciate the show and end up delighted and surprised by how many you do.
Yet its awkward housing at the austere Coliseum exacerbates this 2015 work’s major flaw: reaching for profundity in a skin-deep, conflict-lite tale, instead of enjoying the party.
If the show had as much heart as it has rhythm, it would be a winner.
Finally, the audience at On Your Feet! is on its feet for an otherwise frequently generic guilty pleasure.
The only gem in a treasure chest of fool's gold was Karen Mann as Gloria's pushy grandmother Consuelo nailing some rare gags with her knowing looks and cheeky demeanour.

cn.t: This energetic jukebox musical delivers infectious Latin-pop hits and vibrant dance numbers, but critics find the book formulaic and dull, with pacing issues that prevent Gloria Estefan's compelling life story from fully connecting.
